josh_cs: Putting together a 1-page handoff for the BetaCo trial kickoff tomorrow. Need a compact "cheat" they can share with Eng — cache / batch / stream + what to monitor. Draft below.

josh_cs: HIGH-LEVEL SUMMARY
- Start with cache-first for repeated prompts, batch for bursty microcalls, streaming for interactive UX. Keep a simple rollback plan.

maya_cs: Love concise. Can you also add a tiny perf checklist so SEs can run a quick verification?

josh_cs: Yep. Added.

josh_cs: HANDOFF DRAFT (customer-facing, one page)
1) Before we go live
- Confirm warm pool >= expected TPS for first 2h. If unsure, start at 1.2x expected and scale down.
- Telemetry: validate latency, 5xx count, cache-hit-rate, batch-size histograms. Owner: platform-observability.
- Tracing sampling: 10% during trial.

2) Cache guidance (simple rules)
- Use prefix caching for repeated prefixes (system prompts or canned intros). If >25% identical starts use prefix cache.
- Suggested TTLs: 5-15 minutes for session-level prompts, 12-24 hours for static system messages.
- Use stale-while-revalidate to avoid UX stalls: serve cached then refresh in background.

Sample curl to test cache behavior:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"status update","cache_key":"betaco_status_v1"}' -i
```
Expected: 200 and header `x-cache: HIT` on second request.

3) Batching (practical knobs)
- When many small requests (<150 tokens) batch to reduce cost. Aim for 100-300ms p50 latency for UI calls.
- Adaptive window recommendation: start at 10ms, backoff to 5ms on high-latency alerts. Max batch sizes: 64 for heavy GPUs, 32 for smaller nodes.

SDK snippet (example):
```js
// pseudocode
client.configureBatching({
  initialWindowMs: 10,
  maxWindowMs: 75,
  maxBatchSize: 64,
  latencySloMs: 300
});
```

4) Streaming best-practices
- Use streaming for chat / live assistant. Flush partial tokens every 40-80ms or on sentence boundary.
- Provide non-stream fallback: if stream drops, retry once after 200ms then call non-stream endpoint.

5) Fallback & rollback
- Fallback chain: prod model -> quantized/fast variant -> smaller-context model.
- Circuit-breaker suggestion: open if 5xx rate > 4% over 60s; cool down 30s.
- Rollback trigger: if p95 latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes -> revert cache TTL to 0 and reduce batch window to 5ms.

6) Quick perf checklist for SEs (run 5-10 min)
- Step A: API smoke: run perf script and record baseline tokens/s and p95 latency. (link to perf script).
- Step B: Cache validation: repeated curl above x3 -> expect HIT on second call.
- Step C: Batch probe: send 200 concurrent small requests during business hours labeled `probe=true` so we can observe batch sizes.
- Step D: Streaming smoke: open a streaming session, send 3 prompts, confirm partial flush arrives within 100ms.

nora_sre: Add note: for Dedicated tenants, set per-tenant cache caps (e.g., max_entries=5000) to avoid noisy neighbors. Also recommend soft eviction on OOM.

sam_eng: For batch probe, tell them to run at low QPS first then scale. Also include the circuit-breaker JSON we use internally:
```json
{"failure_threshold_pct":"4","evaluation_window_ms":"60000","open_duration_ms":"30000"}
```

maya_cs: Add a short feedback loop: we check key metrics daily for first week, then weekly for next 3 weeks. Also send a 1-question NPS at day 7 ("How easy was it to integrate?").

infra-bot: Note: docs updated at commit b8d9a2 in /docs/onboarding/one-pagers.

josh_cs: Thanks — I'll attach this as a one-pager to the kickoff invite and recap TTL/batch choices live. Anyone want to own the follow-up thread to capture customer-selected settings?

maya_cs: I got it. I'll post selected TTLs + batch policy after the call. :star_struck:

nora_sre: One more: recommend enabling trace sampling at 10% only for the first 48 hours, then drop to 1% to control cost.

josh_cs: Done. Final edit: trimmed to single sheet, added owners: maya_cs (CS follow-up), nora_sre (ops), sam_eng (tuning). Good to ship.
